title: Traversal of Work Tape Cells
statement: Let $M$ be a multitape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, and let $n,T,t$ be natural numbers, $z$ a finite Boolean string, $	au$ a work-tape index of $M$, $e$ an eleven-register record, and $p$ an input position. Suppose $1 \le T$, $t \le T$, and the registers of $e$ satisfy $e.nc=n$, $e.z=|z|$, $e.t=T$, $e.i=t\,\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)+\tau(2T+1)$, $e.q=0$ when $t=0$ and $e.q=e.i-\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)$ otherwise, $e.lb=t\,\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)$, and $e.ll=e.tmp=0$. Starting in the program template for work-tape cell $\tau$ at phase $0$, with register values $e.f$ and input position $p$, the program reaches the start of the next work-tape cell; its registers are $e.f$ with $i$ replaced by $e.i+(2T+1)$ and $q$ replaced by $0$ when $t=0$ or by $e.i+(2T+1)-\mathrm{Str}(M,n,z,T)$ otherwise, while the input position remains $p$. During this computation it appends the concatenation, over $j=e.i,e.i+1,\ldots,e.i+2T$, of the bit strings generated by the tabulated instruction at index $j$, and takes at most $(2T+3)(\mathrm{Lmax}(M)+20)$ steps.
